<reason>Side B won by turning the motion's own word — "refuse" — into a live, unresolved burden. B's dilemma was consistent and never fully answered: either the platform adjudicates the opt-out (in which case PRO's decade-of-bad-faith indictment applies to its own remedy, "you cannot indict the gatekeeper and then hand him the gate") or the worker self-certifies (the hostile-courier problem). A's answers drifted across rounds — the review gates the system, then it suspends the score's power over access, then it's a novel instrument-examining hearing — and B documented each shift effectively (B4.5, B5.2). A landed real punches: the "safety channel wired to a landmine" reframe and the discrimination-law analogy against the slippery-slope objection were sharp, and A's pressure Q1 on the star's informational content was excellent. But B's A1 answer (stars accumulate across unconnected riders; the star is the tripwire, investigation the response) convincingly absorbed that pressure. B's enforcement-symmetry argument — same compulsion, aim at the bias-causing customers rather than the thermometer, with auditable code changes versus discretionary reviews — survived A's reversal attempt (A4.6) because B showed the filtering is publishable and auditable while volume makes platform review default to denial. A's closing inference ("a rating that can't be trusted to punish can't be trusted as a mandatory foundation") was its best crystallization but leaned on a concession B had coherently reframed. Both sides suffered clipped turns; both followed Q/A format properly. B made the debate easier to decide and held the stronger burden story throughout.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B2.1-B2.3: B seized on A's "threshold review, exactly like the one platforms already run" to force the definitional dilemma — PRO's remedy either isn't a refusal at all or reopens the hostile-courier problem — capped by "You cannot say 'platforms have had a decade and done nothing' and then hand platforms the gatekey." A never cleanly escaped this bind, and B4.1's tripwire answer to A's best pressure question sealed the safety-signal clash.</best_rebuttal>
